Consult Summary:
26-year-old man with known asthma presents via telehealth with 3-hour history of chest tightness, mild shortness of breath, wheeze and dry cough following a recent viral URI; has been without his preventer and reliever inhalers for one week. Clinical impression is an acute mild-to-moderate asthma exacerbation; prescriptions for salbutamol, Clenil Modulite, a 5-day course of oral steroids, and a spacer issued with safety-net advice.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Acute asthma exacerbation
- Onset: 3 hours of chest tightness; feels unable to take full breath.
- Associated symptoms: mild dyspnea on exertion, wheeze, dry cough; no chest pain, no sputum production, no dyspnea at rest.
- Recent precipitant: viral upper-respiratory infection last week (sore throat, runny nose now improving).
- Risk factors: history of severe asthma hospitalization with intubation at age 16-17; non-adherence last week due to running out of inhalers.
- Plan: Restart salbutamol PRN, Clenil Modulite BID (dose not documented), 5-day oral prednisolone (2 tablets each morning, exact dose not documented), supply spacer, red-flag advice if reliever needed more often than every 3 hours or symptoms worsen.

Issue 2: Medication non-adherence / supply lapse
- Patient ran out of both salbutamol and Clenil one week ago while away at university.
- Plan: Electronic prescriptions sent within the hour; education on continued daily preventer use; advised to keep medication supply up to date.

Issue 3: Allergic rhinitis / atopy
- History of hay fever; environmental (dust) allergy.
- Family history: mother eczema, father asthma; patient had childhood eczema and milk-protein allergy.
- No current management requested today.

Medications:
- Salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented (reliever).
- Clenil Modulite (beclomethasone) inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented (preventer).
- Prednisolone tablets – “2 tablets each morning for 5 days” (exact dose not documented) prescribed today.
- Spacer device supplied.

Allergies:
- Environmental: dust mite.
- No known drug allergies.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma (hospitalized with severe exacerbation age 16-17).
- Hay fever.
- Childhood eczema.
- Childhood milk-protein allergy (resolved).

Social History:
- University student; no details on smoking, alcohol, or living arrangements documented.

Preventative History:
- No information provided on vaccinations, cancer screening, or other preventive care.

Physical Examination:
- Telehealth consult; no vitals or physical findings documented.

Plan:
- Electronic prescriptions for salbutamol, Clenil Modulite, spacer, and 5-day prednisolone.
- Patient education: spacer technique; resume preventer inhaler daily; use salbutamol PRN; seek immediate medical care if reliever required >q3h, worsening breathlessness, chest pain, light-headedness.
- Rest from work/study as needed; self-certify up to 7 days.
- Consider follow-up review if symptoms persist beyond steroid course or sooner if deteriorating.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing expected elements: smoking status, alcohol use, vaccination/screening status, vital signs, objective respiratory assessment (e.g., peak flow).  
● No internal conflicts noted.  
● Transcript quality: generally clear; minor audio dropouts but did not obscure clinical content.
